book: Maha-bharata, The Epic of Ancient India Condensed into English Verse (Romesh C. Dutt)

chunks.why: Pandavas honored as god-born princes at Drona's tournament; Karna arrives as jealous rival to Arjun.
Karna crowned; Duryodhan's fire-plot forces exile disguised as Brahmans, journeying hopefully to Draupadi's swayamvara.
Arjun wins Draupadi, Krishna quells suitors' mob; brothers granted Indra-prastha, Yudhishthir begins Rajasuya.
Rajasuya triumph: Yudhishthir crowned emperor, all monarchs pay tribute, Krishna slays scoffing Sisupala.
Yudhishthir loses everything at rigged dice; Draupadi dragged and insulted; brothers stripped, sent into exile.
Vidura's parting blessing, Pritha's anguished farewell; exiled brothers enter jungle life listening to Savitri tale.
Still in forest exile; Markandeya narrates Savitri's story to console grieving Yudhishthir over Draupadi's suffering.
Savitri conquers Yama; Pandavas hidden as menials in Virata's court; Kurus raid, Arjun as Brihannala arms for battle.
Arjun defeats Kuru host, recovers cattle, reveals identity; Abhimanyu weds Virata's princess amid feast and gifts.
Krishna sues for peace at Hastina; Duryodhan haughtily refuses to yield even needle-point of land, war inevitable.
War joined; Bhishma scatters Pandavas day one, Arjun rallies day two; heavy carnage on both sides.
Bhishma keeps routing Pandavs; son Iravat slain; strategy set to fell Bhishma using Sikhandin.
Bhishma falls on bed of arrows, big tactical victory; Abhimanyu enters battle as Drona takes command.
Abhimanyu slaughtered by six chiefs; Arjun avenges on Jayadratha but Bhima's son Ghatotkacha killed by Karna.
Drupad and Virata slain; Yudhishthir's half-lie fells Drona; Karna takes command, Yudhishthir routed and shamed.
Karna, Salya slain; Bhima breaks Duryodhan's thigh; Aswa-thaman's midnight raid slaughters Draupadi's five sons.
Mass funeral rites; Gandhari's lament; Kunti reveals Karna was their eldest brother, Yudhishthir crushed by grief.
Yudhishthir performs Aswa-medha; Arjun's conquering horse returns; universal recognition and bounty restore glory.
Ascent to heaven: Yudhishthir reunited with brothers, Karna, Draupadi as immortals, all glorified in celestial realm.
Translator's epilogue; story concluded with Pandavas transcended to heaven, their names venerated across ages.
